title: Where are Salinas Valley's haunted places? A guide to 5 local legends
excerpt: From lonely backroads to historic landmarks, the Salinas Valley is full of ghostly stories passed down for generations. Take a tour of the Valley's most talked-about haunted places.
content:
Oct. 15, 2026, 3:01 a.m. PT

From quiet backroads to historic landmarks, a handful of places across Salinas and Monterey County have become woven into local lore through stories of unexplained figures, strange sounds and alleged ghostly encounters.

The tales stretch from the intersection of Crazy Horse Canyon and Old Stage roads to Fremont Peak, Los Coches Adobe in Soledad and even the boyhood home of John Steinbeck. Over the years, residents have shared their own versions of these stories, helping turn them into fixtures of the region's Halloween folklore.

Though unverified, the legends persist, whispered around campfires, shared on late-night drives and passed along as local lore. Here's a geographic guide to some of the Salinas Valley's most enduring ghost stories and haunted legends.

Crazy Horse Canyon and Old Stage roads: La Llorona

Few local legends are as enduring as the stories tied to the intersection of Crazy Horse Canyon Road and Old Stage Road, where some residents say they've encountered La Llorona, the Wailing Woman.

In the versions passed down locally, a mysterious woman appears along the roadside late at night. Some say she's searching for her husband. Others claim she was killed in the area.

Emmanuel Casas told the newsroom in 2019 that the figure appeared dressed as a bride and vanished whenever anyone tried to get close.

"If you try to get out, she disappears," Casas said.

But that's not the version Daisy Vega grew up hearing.

"She just appears in the rear view mirror," Vega said. "But when you turn around, she isn't there."

Vega said the story feels right at home on a road known for its darkness, blind turns and isolated feel, features that have long contributed to its reputation as one of the area's spookier stretches.

Fremont Peak: Shadows crossing the road

High above the valley, Fremont Peak has inspired its own collection of unexplained stories, including reports of shadowy figures darting across the roadway before seemingly vanishing.

One of the more striking accounts came from Lisa Rodriguez, who recalled an encounter at Fremont Peak around sunset in 2019. Two drivers traveling in opposite directions reportedly witnessed the same unexplained sight: something running across the road and vanishing into the mountainside.

"There were two cars," Rodriguez said, "one going up and one going down at sunset. We saw something run across the road and disappear into the face of the mountain − we slammed on the brakes and so did the other car."

When both vehicles stopped, Rodriguez said, whatever they had seen was gone.

Los Coches Adobe in Soledad: A figure in black

Few places in Monterey County carry as many dark legends as Los Coches Adobe, a former inn and stagecoach stop in Soledad.

Over the years, visitors have described strange experiences inside the historic building, including the feeling that they've somehow stepped back into another era. But the adobe's most infamous tale centers on a woman said to have operated an inn or brothel there and allegedly murdered overnight guests for their gold.

Author Randall A. Reinstedt included a version of the story in "Ghostly Tales and Mysterious Happenings of Old Monterey." In that account, the woman killed sleeping miners and disposed of their bodies in a nearby mine shaft.

Other stories tell of a figure dressed in black appearing inside the adobe, while some visitors have reported waking with the sensation that an unseen presence was pressing on their chest. As with the other accounts in this guide, none has been verified.

Steinbeck House: A silhouette at the window

Even the Steinbeck House has earned a place in local ghost lore.

The legend may have gained its biggest boost from John Steinbeck himself. In a letter, the famed author wrote that the Salinas home was haunted and that he had seen things walking through the house at night, though available accounts do not say exactly what he believed he saw.

Later, author Randall A. Reinstedt wrote that employees at the Steinbeck House had reported seeing a silhouette near a downstairs window. He also recounted three reported sightings in the 1970s of a profile-like figure shrouded in a yellowish mist.

Another story centers on a Hartnell College student who spent a night in what had once been Steinbeck's bedroom. The student reportedly heard a door opening and closing and sensed someone else in the room. But when the student looked around, no one was there.

Salinas schools: Bell-tower voices and a poolside figure

Ghost stories aren't limited to historic buildings and lonely roads. Some of Salinas' best-known legends have unfolded on school campuses, where tales of unexplained encounters have circulated among students for years.

At Salinas High School, stories passed from one generation to the next include reports of unexplained voices and paranormal activity around the bell tower.

At Alisal High School, a video that surfaced in 2009 appeared to show a white figure moving back and forth near the school pool. While the footage sparked plenty of speculation, it never established what the figure actually was.

Salinas Californian archives contributed to this report.
